page.title: Settings
page.description: Configure the console's appearance, notifications and security.

unreachable.title: Couldn't read this appliance's configuration
unreachable.description: The appliance could not load its settings. The values below may be defaults or outdated. You cannot save changes until the settings load again.

toast.connectLive: Connect to a live appliance to use this.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.description: Tune the console to your taste. Theme applies instantly; the rest saves with the section.

language.label: Language
language.description: The display language for the console.

theme.label: Theme
theme.description: Dark by default — the appliance is happiest at night.

accent.label: Accent
accent.description: The highlight colour for selected states and focus.

density.label: Density
density.description: Compact tightens table rows and spacing.

reduceMotion.label: Reduce motion
reduceMotion.description: Minimize animations and transitions throughout the console.

autoCollapse.label: Auto-collapse sidebar
autoCollapse.description: Collapse the navigation rail to icons on narrower windows.

jobFailure.label: Job failure
jobFailure.blurb: A backup run fails or errors

access.title: Access & policy
access.description: Change the password for your account.

session.title: Session duration
session.description: How long a sign-in stays active before you're asked to sign in again.
session.label: Stay signed in for
session.hint: Applies immediately to this session, and to future sign-ins on this browser.

applyFailed.title: Session duration not applied
applyFailed.description: Saved locally, but the appliance couldn't be reached — it'll apply next time you sign in.

certificate.title: HTTPS certificate
certificate.description: The certificate this console and the REST API are served with. Both are only reachable over HTTPS; plain HTTP requests are redirected.
certificate.loadFailed: Couldn't read the certificate from the appliance.
certificate.sourceGenerated: Generated by this appliance and renewed automatically before it expires. Browsers show an untrusted-certificate warning for it until you install one from a trusted certificate authority.
certificate.sourceInstalled: Installed by {{user}} on {{when}}. It is not renewed automatically — install a replacement before it expires.
certificate.sourceManual: Placed on the appliance by hand. It is not renewed automatically — install a replacement before it expires.

warning.expired: This certificate has expired. Browsers refuse it without an explicit override — install a new one.
warning.expiresSoon_one: This certificate expires in {{count}} day and is not renewed automatically.
warning.expiresSoon_other: This certificate expires in {{count}} days and is not renewed automatically.
warning.expiresSoonAutoRenew_one: This certificate expires in {{count}} day; the appliance renews it automatically.
warning.expiresSoonAutoRenew_other: This certificate expires in {{count}} days; the appliance renews it automatically.
warning.noNames: The certificate lists no host names or IP addresses (subject alternative names). Browsers ignore the common name, so they reject it for every address.
warning.namesNotCovered: None of this appliance's own names or addresses ({{names}}) are in the certificate. Browsers will warn unless the console is opened through a name the certificate lists.

toast.reloaded: New connections already use it. Reload this page to switch this browser over.
toast.nextStart: Saved. The appliance serves it from its next restart.

revertDialog.title: Revert to a self-signed certificate?
revertDialog.description: The installed certificate and its key are removed, and the appliance generates a new self-signed certificate and serves it right away. Browsers will show an untrusted-certificate warning again, and CLI clients that trusted the current key will need to trust the new one.

form.title: Install a certificate
form.intro: Use a certificate issued by your certificate authority, or your own self-signed one. The appliance checks the pair before replacing anything, so a mistake leaves the current certificate in place.
form.certificateHint: The server certificate first, then any intermediate certificates. A combined .pem file that also holds the key fills both fields.
form.privateKeyHint: RSA (2048 bits or more) or EC (P-256, P-384, P-521). Stored on the appliance, readable only by its service.
form.passphraseHint: Only for an encrypted key. Used once to read it and not stored.
form.fileTooLarge: {{name}} is too large to be a PEM certificate or key.
form.fileNotPem: {{name}} has no PEM certificate or private key in it. Convert DER or PKCS#12 (.pfx) files to PEM first.
form.privateKeyRequired: Paste or load the private key.
form.installFailed: The appliance couldn't install this certificate.
form.afterInstall: New connections get the certificate straight away. CLI clients that trusted the previous key will refuse to connect until they trust the new one.

operator.label: Operator
operator.blurb: Run jobs & restores; no policy changes

users.title: Users
users.description: People who can sign in to this appliance and what they may do.

removeUser.title: Remove {{name}}?
removeUser.description: They'll immediately lose access to this appliance. Their audit history is retained. This can't be undone.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.description: Credentials for the AltaStor API, CLI and integrations.

empty.title: No API tokens
empty.description: Create a token to authenticate the API, CLI or Terraform provider.

revokeToken.title: Revoke {{name}}?
revokeToken.description: Any client using this token will immediately lose access. This can't be undone.

keyEscrow.title: Encryption key escrow
keyEscrow.description: A copy of your backup encryption keys that survives this appliance.
keyEscrow.warning: Keys for encrypted backups live only in this appliance's catalog. Lose the catalog and those restore points can't be decrypted — even though the data is safe in the repository. Export regularly and keep the archive somewhere else.
keyEscrow.passwordHint: At least {{count}} characters. It's the only thing protecting the keys and credentials inside the archive.

toast.doneDescription: {{jobs}} jobs and {{backups}} backups, with their encryption keys. Store it off this appliance.
toast.failedDescription: The appliance didn't produce an archive. Try again in a moment.

appliance.title: Backup server
appliance.probeFailed: Couldn't read hardware details from the appliance. Fields it reports are shown as “—”.

createToken.copyDescription: This is the only time the full token is shown. Store it somewhere safe.
createToken.createDescription: Tokens authenticate the AltaStor API and CLI. Scope them to the minimum needed.
createToken.treatLikePassword: Treat it like a password. Anyone with this token can act as <0>{{scope}}</0> client.

inviteUser.title: Invite user
inviteUser.description: They'll receive an invitation to set a password and enrol MFA.
inviteUser.name: Full name

users.title: Users
users.description: Who can sign in, and the one role each of them holds.
users.lastAdminNote: Disabling a user signs them out everywhere. The last enabled Administrator can't be demoted, disabled or deleted, so someone can always manage users.

form.title: Add user
form.description: The user signs in with this name and password, and can do what the role allows.
form.name: User name

deleteDialog.title: Delete {{name}}?
deleteDialog.description: The user is signed out everywhere and can no longer sign in. Their entries in the audit log stay.

roles.title: Roles & permissions
roles.description: What each built-in role allows, function by function. Anything not allowed is disabled.
roles.builtInNote: The roles are built in and can't be changed or deleted.
